messages:
alex: Heads-up — I saw a weird batching regression in the staging cluster when prefix-hit ratio climbs above ~60%. Latency p50 for short prompts jumped ~18% even though token throughput looked fine. Anyone else?

maya: Yikes. Seen anything in profiler? kernel selection or packing changes recently? :thinking: 

dmitri: We recently landed the kernel-route fallback that adds a quick compatibility check per-batch. Microbenchmarks said +40us, but on real traffic that might amplify. I can pull traces.

sophie: I captured a few traces from the affected node group. Two things stood out: (1) many tiny batches are being formed with <4 active tokens because KV-cache hits reduce token demand, (2) the batcher still tries to greedily pack hits together which delays miss-heavy queues.

alex: here's a short profiler snippet (sampled):
```
# sample: avg per-batch overhead (ns)
before: 70_000
after: 200_000  # after kernel-route fallback
hot path: packer.sched -> select_kernel -> run
```

maya: So the kernel-route check added ~130us/batch. If cache-hit packing increases batch count, that multiplies. That explains p50 rise even if tokens/sec stable.

dmitri: Agree. Two levers: reduce per-batch kernel checks (memoize more aggressively for recent model & shape), or change queue policy to avoid making so many tiny batches when hit-heavy traffic dominates.

sophie: I prototyped a queue tweak: hit-aware admission that treats a hit as 0.25 of token weight for the token budget when packing. Effectively: token_cost = tokens * (is_hit ? 0.25 : 1.0). This reduces tiny-hit-only batches and lets misses join sooner. Quick numbers from local sim: p50 latency down 12% vs current, tokens/sec same, tail unaffected.

alex: Nice. Can you paste the pseudo-config?

sophie: config snippet I used: 
```
batcher:
  token_budget: 1536
  hit_token_factor: 0.25  # weight multiplier for prefix/KV-cache hits
  max_batch_delay_ms: 12
  allow_mixed_miss_priority: true
```

maya: how does that interact with canary kernel-route memoization? If we still do per-batch checks, we still pay overhead.

dmitri: With hit_token_factor, batch count drops so overall kernel checks apply to fewer batches. But we should still memoize select_kernel by (model, seq_len_bucket, device) keys for O(1) lookup. I'll add a small LRU keyed by (model, seq_sum_bin).

alex: Any regressions from quality or cost? We need to ensure hit_factor doesn't overpack and raise memory/KV pressure.

sophie: I simulated hot prefix skew where 80% hits come from long prefix contexts; turned hit_token_factor to 0.5 in that sim and memory stayed within limits. Suggest exposing hit_token_factor as a per-model tunable with safe bounds [0.1, 1.0].

maya: Good. Can we run a short A/B in staging: route 10% traffic to variant with hit_token_factor=0.25 + memoized kernel select? We should capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, kernel-check-count.

dmitri: I'll wire an experiment flag. infra-bot: deploy scheduled for 2026-03-19 03:00 UTC to staging (canary=10%).

infra-bot: Deployment created: redwood/staging/packet-197-kv-packer-expt. Canary=10%. Metric hooks: /metrics/batcher/p50, /metrics/kernelselect/count, /metrics/tokens/s.

alex: Thanks. One more ask — add a debug histogram for "effective_batch_token_weight" so we can see how hit weighting affects batch sizes in production.

sophie: will do. Also logging a sample of 1/10k batches with fields: is_mixed, hits_count, misses_count, effective_token_weight, kernel_memo_hit.

maya: ack. Let's reconvene after 6 hours of canary and check the dashboards. If we see kernel-check-count drop and p50 improve, we promote.

dmitri: plan: (1) add memo LRU for select_kernel, (2) add hit_token_factor tunable and default 0.3 for staging expt, (3) add hist/logging, (4) run canary 10% for 6h. I'll open a small PR and reference this thread.

alex: perfect. Tag me on the PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
